test_title: SSC MTS 2024 Official Paper (Held On: 11 Nov, 2024 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
solution:
The correct answer is '**ourselves**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In this sentence, the word "ourselves" is used as a reflexive pronoun, which is correct because the ability to express clearly and confidently refers to the subject "we" or "ourselves" in this context.
 
• "Ourselves" is the correct reflexive pronoun to use when the subject of the sentence is plural and includes the speaker, as in this case where "we" are the implied subject of the ability to express clearly and confidently.
 
• Other options like "**itself**", "**themselves**", and "**herself**" are incorrect because they refer to singular or gender-specific subjects, which do not match the plural subject implied in this sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is '**Option 2**'.

 

Complete Passage: *Speaking is a powerful tool ***(1) *for *__***human communication. It allows us to convey thoughts, emotions and ideas to others. Effective speaking * **(2) __*involves *__***not only the words we choose but also our tone, body language and overall presentation. Public speaking, in particular, can be ***(3) *__both __****a skill and an art, enabling individuals to inspire, educate and persuade audiences. ***(4) *__Whether __****it is a casual conversation with a friend or a formal presentation to a large group, the ability to express ***(5) *__ourselves __****clearly and confidently through speaking is a valuable skill that can greatly impact our personal and professional lives.*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• "Itself" refers to a singular subject, which does not fit the plural context of "we" or "ourselves".
 
• "Themselves" is a reflexive pronoun used for plural subjects, but it refers to a group other than the speaker, making it incorrect here.
 
• "Herself" refers to a singular feminine subject, which is not appropriate in this context as the sentence refers to "we" as the implied subject.
